extracted.intended_audience: listeners, donors, public radio stakeholders, journalists, and policymakers
extracted.subtask_description: An institutional overview of NPR's financial model, public funding context, and transparency practices, including available audited statements and tax filings, plus appeals for listener support. It frames the funding rationale and the organization's responsibilities to audiences and funders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Organizational independence and nonprofit status
rubrics_metrics.description: “NPR is an independent, non-profit media organization. We are also a membership organization made up of independently operated public radio stations — in all 50 states, as well as the District of Columbia, Guam and the U.S. Virgin Islands — that together reach more than 99% of Americans.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasizes NPR's independent nonprofit structure and distributed membership network as foundational to its operations and reach.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mission and editorial commitment
rubrics_metrics.description: “NPR and its remarkable network of local stations will continue to bring you rigorous journalism, courageous storytelling, inspired music discovery, and the kind of reporting that democracy depends on — every day, without fear or favor. That is the promise of a free press in a democracy. It's in the First Amendment. It is the mission of public media.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Positions editorial independence, rigorous journalism, and service to democracy as core obligations that funding supports.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mixed private-public funding model is essential
rubrics_metrics.description: “Federal funding and direct support from listeners and readers are both critical pieces of the private-public funding model that has made public media possible from the very beginning.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Frames both federal appropriations and individual listener/reader contributions as complementary and necessary components of public media finance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cost-per-capita framing of public media funding
rubrics_metrics.description: “All for about $1.60 per American, every year.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Uses a simple per-person metric to contextualize the scale and public value of federal support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Service scope supported by funding
rubrics_metrics.description: “It supports access to news and information, educational resources, noncommercial music, and emergency alerting services for the entire nation — particularly in rural and underserved areas where commercial media organizations can't or won't compete.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Articulates the public goods (news, education, music, emergency alerting) that federal and listener funding enable, with emphasis on rural and underserved communities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Federal funding is a very small share of total federal spending
rubrics_metrics.description: “Federal funding for public media also only amounted to about 0.01% of federal spending, but it supported services in communities across America.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides proportional context to counter perceptions about the budgetary impact of public media funding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Leverage effect of federal grants
rubrics_metrics.description: “For every federal grant dollar received, on average, public radio stations have been able to leverage those funds to raise seven times the amount from other sources such as local listener, foundation, and business support.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Presents a quantitative leverage metric (1:7) to demonstrate the catalytic impact of federal grants on local fundraising.

rubrics_metrics.name: Call to action / interim reliance on listener support
rubrics_metrics.description: “We will fight to restore federal funding. In the meantime, support from listeners and readers is more critical than ever.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Positions advocacy for federal funding alongside immediate appeals for individual financial support as a practical strategy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Availability of Annual Reports and historical publication practice
rubrics_metrics.description: “NPR's annual report shares highlights from our work over the past year, made possible by the generosity of our community of supporters. NPR has published its annual reports since 2001.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Signals ongoing public reporting of institutional highlights and a continuity of annual disclosure since 2001.

rubrics_metrics.name: Audited consolidated financial statements (availability and caveat)
rubrics_metrics.description: Lists audited consolidated financial statements for FY2021 / FY2022 / FY2023 / FY2024 / FY2025 and states: “The audited consolidated financial statements are presented for convenience and information purposes only. While reasonable efforts have been made to ensure the integrity of such information, the audited consolidated financial statements presented should not be relied upon. An official printed copy of audited consolidated financial statements will be provided upon request.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides public access to audited statements online but disclaims reliance on the posted versions and offers official printed copies on request—indicating a transparency standard plus a legal/accuracy caveat.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public availability of IRS Form 990 and 990-T filings
rubrics_metrics.description: Enumerates IRS Form 990 Filings for NPR, Inc.; NPR Foundation; American Coalition for Public Radio; NPR International Operations, Inc. for FY2021–FY2024, and IRS Form 990-T Filings for the same entities for FY2021–FY2024.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Demonstrates tax-reporting transparency by publishing annual IRS filings for NPR and affiliated entities, enabling public review of nonprofit tax disclosures and unrelated business income returns.
